record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: For Informational Statistical Thermodynamics, can one determine the sign of the local-in-space IST entropy production density appearing in the entropy balance equation, rather than only proving a weak global non-negative informational-entropy production principle for the total IST entropy increase along a nonequilibrium trajectory?

evidence.quote: Finally, at present we cannot make any definitive statement on the sign of the local in space IST-entropy production density of Eq. (53).
However. it is possible to derive what we call a weak principle of non-negative informational-entropy production.

which is an expression indicating that the global IST-entropy of the dissipative system always increases in time, from its initial value, along the trajectory of evolution of the nonequilibrium macrostate of the system.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a many-body open dissipative system described within a nonequilibrium statistical ensemble formalism built on the maximum-entropy principle (MaxEnt-NESOM). The macroscopic nonequilibrium state of the system is specified by a basic set of dynamical variables {P_j(r)} (densities of energy, particle number, momentum, and possibly higher-order fluxes and tensors), whose averages and conjugate intensive nonequilibrium thermodynamic variables {F_j(r,t)} are obtained from a generalized Gibbs-like statistical operator constructed by maximizing the Gibbs informational entropy subject to constraints fixing those averages at each time t.

The Informational Statistical Thermodynamic (IST) entropy is defined as
   S(t) = -Tr{ ρ̄(t,0) ln ρ̄(t,0) },
where ρ̄(t,0) is the auxiliary (instantaneously "frozen") MaxEnt operator. One may write S(t) as a spatial integral of a local IST entropy density s(r,t), and the time derivative obeys a local balance equation
   ∂_t s(r,t) + ∇·J_s(r,t) = σ(r,t),
where J_s is an entropy flux and σ(r,t) is the local IST entropy production density.

It is known that a "weak principle of non-negative informational-entropy production" can be established, asserting that the global IST entropy satisfies
   S(t) ≥ S(t_0)   for all t ≥ t_0
along the trajectory of evolution of the nonequilibrium macrostate, i.e. the spatially integrated production ∫ σ(r,t) d³r leads to a non-decreasing global IST entropy.

Question: Can one determine the sign of the local-in-space IST entropy production density σ(r,t) itself — that is, establish (or refute) a pointwise inequality σ(r,t) ≥ 0 for all r and all t in the evolution of the nonequilibrium macrostate — going beyond the weak global statement of non-negativity of the total IST entropy increase?
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on MaxEnt-NESOM/IST consistently reports only a weak (global) principle of non-negative informational entropy production; no general result determining the pointwise sign of the local IST entropy production density appears to have been established. Recent related work (e.g., on inferring entropy production in many-body systems via nonequilibrium MaxEnt, 2025) addresses bounds and hierarchical decompositions but does not resolve the local-sign question within the IST framework.

status_evidence.snippet: discusses MaxEnt entropy and entropy production, as well as a weak principle of positive entropy production
status_evidence.claim: Only a weak (global) principle of non-negative entropy production is established in IST.
